conversation.content:
Hello! My name is Dr. Martinez, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived—this is routine care, not a test of your parenting. We’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), a short, 10-question screener that helps us understand the emotional ups and downs many new moms experience. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell me someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers; we just want to know what the past seven days have felt like for you. Ready to begin?

First question: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?

Honestly, laughing feels pretty hard these days. I’ll smile if someone shows me a cute video or if my husband tries to be silly, but it’s like the sound won’t quite come out. Most of the time I’m too tired or worried to find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… I mean, I can smile when my husband makes a goofy face at the baby, but actually laughing—like the kind that comes from your belly—hasn’t happened much. Everything just feels heavy, so even funny things feel kind of “meh.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much lately. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk around the lake—but now it feels like, “What’s the point?” I still go through the motions for the baby’s sake, but that spark of “can’t wait” just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot. If she’s fussy, I immediately think it’s something I ate or that I’m not soothing her right. When I couldn’t get her to latch yesterday, I sat there crying, telling myself I’m already failing her. Even little stuff—like the laundry piling up—feels like proof I’m not keeping it together.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. I’ll be sitting on the couch, baby’s sleeping fine, but my chest feels tight like something bad’s about to happen. I check her breathing every ten minutes, and if she makes one weird sound I’m googling fevers or rashes at 2 a.m. I know people say it’s normal new-mom worry, but it feels bigger—like I can’t shut it off even when everything looks okay.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes, yeah. It’s like a sudden wave—my heart races, I feel shaky, and I’m sure something awful is about to happen even though nothing’s wrong. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days feel like I’m drowning in small stuff. Feeding, changing, trying to sleep, then the cycle starts again. I’ll look at the sink full of bottles and just want to sit on the floor and cry because I don’t know which task to tackle first. I still get everything done—somehow—but it feels like I’m barely treading water the whole time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah, that’s been happening. Even when the baby’s finally down and the house is quiet, my mind keeps spinning—did I sterilize the bottles right, is she gaining enough weight, am I already messing her up? I’ll lie there for an hour or two before I drift off, then any little whimper snaps me awake. It’s like I can’t turn the worry switch off long enough to stay asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the time, honestly. I wake up feeling like there’s this gray cloud hanging over me. I’ll see the sun out the window, but it doesn’t seem to reach me. Little things make me tear up—like a diaper commercial or when the baby stares at me and I think, “Does she deserve a happier mom?” I keep waiting for the sadness to lift, but it just sits there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s been happening a few times a week. Sometimes it’s over obvious stuff, like when she won’t settle and I feel useless, but other times it’s for no clear reason—just this heaviness that spills out. I’ll be folding her tiny clothes and suddenly the tears start. I try to keep it quiet so my husband doesn’t worry, but it’s hard to stop once it starts.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel low and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can take care of my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, 0–6 weeks post-delivery (exact days not specified)  
Date: ________   Screener: ________  

Symptoms endorsed (EPDS-relevant):  
- Anhedonia, pervasive low mood, frequent tearfulness (Q1, Q2, Q8, Q9)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt; feelings of incompetence as a mother (Q3)  
- Persistent, intrusive anxiety and panic episodes with somatic arousal (Q4, Q5)  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed, “drowning,” difficulty prioritizing tasks (Q6)  
- Sleep disturbance clearly linked to rumination and worry, not solely infant needs (Q7)  

Pattern: Symptoms present “most of the time,” cause functional impairment (completes tasks but with significant distress), no periods of elevated mood or psychotic content reported.

Safety: Denies any thoughts of self-harm or harm to infant (Q10). No current suicidal ideation.

Risk factors of screening significance  
- Moderate–high likelihood of major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety  
- Maternal distress sufficient to impair bonding and daily functioning  
- No protective report of social support beyond spouse (not explored in detail)

Screening impression  
Findings exceed “baby blues” threshold; meet provisional cut-off for possible major postpartum depression ± anxiety disorder. Recommend formal diagnostic assessment and discussion of treatment options at earliest convenience.

End of screening note
